Discrete-Time Model with Individual-Level External Data (Composite Likelihood)

discrete_indi.Rd

Fits a series of grouped-time (discrete-time) survival models to the internal data together with an external cohort's records, one fit per value of the integration weight eta. It is the discrete-time counterpart of cox_indi().

Usage

discrete_indi(
  z_int,
  delta_int,
  interval_int,
  stratum_int = NULL,
  z_ext,
  delta_ext,
  interval_ext,
  stratum_ext = NULL,
  etas,
  link = c("cloglog", "logit"),
  n_intervals = NULL,
  tol = 1e-09,
  Mstop = 200,
  message = FALSE
)

Arguments

z_int, delta_int, interval_int, stratum_int

The internal cohort: covariates, event indicator, last interval at risk and optional strata (see discretekl()).

z_ext, delta_ext, interval_ext, stratum_ext

The external cohort, in the same form, with the internal covariate names.

etas

Numeric vector of non-negative integration weights; sorted in ascending order.

link

"cloglog" (complementary log-log: the grouped proportional-hazards model, the default, on the scale of a Cox model's coefficients) or "logit" (proportional odds of the interval hazard).

n_intervals

Number of intervals \(K\); defaults to the largest interval in either cohort.

tol

Convergence tolerance of the Fisher-scoring iterations. Default 1e-9.

Mstop

Maximum number of iterations per fit. Default 200.

message

Logical; if TRUE, prints a progress bar.

Value

An object of class "discrete_indi": as discretekl(), with the linear predictors of the internal subjects in linear.predictors_int; gamma holds the internal baseline.

Details

The objective (minimized) is the composite likelihood $$-\frac{1}{n_{int}}\{\ell_{int}(\gamma, \beta) + \eta\, \ell_{ext}(\gamma^{ext}, \beta)\},$$ in which the two cohorts share the coefficients \(\beta\) and each keeps its own baseline hazard (its own \(\gamma\) per stratum and interval). External records carry weight eta; eta = 0 is the internal model alone. The external records must use the internal covariate names and the same intervals.

See also

cv.discrete_indi(), discrete_indi_ridge(), discrete_indi_enet()

Examples

data(ExampleData_discrete)
tr <- ExampleData_discrete$train; ex <- ExampleData_discrete$external
fit <- discrete_indi(z_int = tr$z, delta_int = tr$status, interval_int = tr$interval,
                     z_ext = ex$z, delta_ext = ex$status, interval_ext = ex$interval,
                     etas = c(0, 0.1, 1))
fit$beta
#>             0         0.1           1
#> Z1  0.5812913  0.64073489  0.68043980
#> Z2 -0.7813239 -0.57441011 -0.48044118
#> Z3  0.9250432  0.65037230  0.58689256
#> Z4 -1.2837399 -0.71279721 -0.33278501
#> Z5  0.1817395  0.27066409  0.35534976
#> Z6 -0.1391096 -0.07379986 -0.01634817
